sop_modules.name: Exterior Masonry Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape/hardscape protection, mask light fixtures and HVAC units, set up access equipment and spray rigs. Window/door glass protection is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in window/door specs.

tasks.name: Landscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent to masonry wall. Measured in linear feet along the foundation/masonry wall line. Full cover for spray_backroll (10-15 ft overspray drift), edge tarps for roll-only.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of plantings within spray drift zone. Secure tarps against wind with stakes or weights. UV-resistant 4 mil plastic minimum for multi-day masonry projects.

tasks.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over walkways, patios, and driveways adjacent to masonry wall.

quality_notes.all: Tape plastic to foundation at grade line using red stucco tape for masonry surfaces. Extend coverage to overspray zone. Canvas for crew traffic areas (non-slip).

tasks.name: Fixture and HVAC Masking
tasks.description: Mask exterior light fixtures with tape and plastic bags. Bag and tarp HVAC condenser units if adjacent to masonry wall. Use blue masking tape on smooth fixture/HVAC surfaces — stucco tape not needed on non-masonry surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all fixtures and utility connections on working elevation. Do not block HVAC intake/exhaust if unit is running. Secure plastic with weights — wind can dislodge loose covering.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Configure airless sprayer: 517 tip + 60-mesh filter for primer/acrylic finish, OR 531 tip + 30-mesh filter for block filler/elastomeric. Stage materials. Stage 18-inch roller frame + 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap covers for mandatory backroll.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size matches material: 517 for acrylic/primer, 531 for block filler/elastomeric. Verify filter mesh: 60-mesh (black) for latex, 30-mesh (gray) for block filler/elastomeric. Stage roller alongside sprayer — backroll is MANDATORY on all masonry spray operations. Two-person crew minimum.

tasks.name: Roll/Brush Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Stage rollers (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap for masonry), brushes, trays, extension poles, and materials.

quality_notes.all: Stage enough material for full elevation run. Extension poles for elevated work. Thick-nap roller covers (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch) are mandatory for masonry texture.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape/hardscape protection first -> Fixture/HVAC masking -> Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Exterior Masonry Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: NC masonry prep: cure verification (28-day standard or 7-day with Loxon primer), moisture testing (MC <12% hard stop), efflorescence treatment (if present), power wash (allowed on masonry — unlike fiber cement), form-release removal (concrete only), caulk masonry-to-trim joints, surface defect repair.

tasks.name: Cure Time Verification
tasks.description: Verify masonry cure status. Standard: 28 days from pour/lay. Accelerated: 7 days minimum when alkali-resistant primer (Loxon-type) is specified. Document cure date from construction schedule. If cure time insufficient, HARD STOP — do not proceed.

quality_notes.all: Verify cure date from GC or construction schedule. Document in project file. 7-day accelerated path REQUIRES alkali-resistant primer — no exceptions.

tasks.name: Moisture Content Testing
tasks.description: Test moisture content of masonry surface. Must read <12% MC before any coating application. Test methods: electronic moisture meter, ASTM D4263 (Plastic Sheet Method), or ASTM F1869 (Calcium Chloride Test). MC >12% is a HARD STOP — do not coat.

quality_notes.QT2: Spot check representative areas on each elevation.
quality_notes.QT3: Check multiple points per elevation. Document readings.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic check grid pattern. All readings documented. Every area must pass <12% MC.

tasks.name: Efflorescence Treatment
tasks.description: Remove efflorescence (white salt deposits) before any coating. Cleaning hierarchy: (1) water + stiff brush (light), (2) TSP solution (moderate), (3) phosphoric acid (severe), (4) muriatic acid 1:10-1:16 dilution (extreme, last resort). IMPORTANT: No acid cleaning on limestone substrate — acid dissolves calcite. Pre-dampen masonry before acid, scrub, neutralize with alkaline solution, rinse thoroughly.

quality_notes.QT2: Brush off loose efflorescence. Water wash.
quality_notes.QT3: Full removal with TSP if moderate. Verify moisture source addressed.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete removal. TSP or acid wash as required. Document treatment and verify no recurrence before coating.

tasks.name: Power Wash Masonry Surface
tasks.description: Power wash masonry wall to remove construction dust, dirt, debris, and loose material. Power washing IS allowed on masonry (unlike fiber cement and engineered wood). Use 1,500-2,500 PSI — sufficient for masonry cleaning without mortar joint damage. Allow 24-48 hr dry time before coating. Verify MC <12% after drying.

quality_notes.QT2: Basic power wash to remove visible dirt and debris.
quality_notes.QT3: Full power wash with detergent. Rinse thoroughly. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.
quality_notes.QT4: Full power wash with TSP solution. Rinse thoroughly. Allow 48 hr dry time minimum. Moisture meter check mandatory before proceeding.

tasks.name: Form-Release Agent Removal
tasks.description: Remove waxy form-release agents and curing compounds from cast concrete surfaces. These are bond-breakers that prevent coating adhesion. Methods: mechanical abrasion, abrasive blasting, or chemical detergents. Applies to cast concrete substrate ONLY — not needed on brick, CMU, or limestone.

quality_notes.all: Water bead test: splash water on surface. If water beads, form-release agent is still present — continue removal. Water should absorb into surface when form-release is fully removed.

tasks.name: Caulk Masonry-to-Trim Joints
tasks.description: Apply polyurethane exterior caulk (Class 25/50) to masonry-to-trim joints: masonry-to-window casings, masonry-to-door casings, masonry-to-soffit transitions. Use red stucco tape for masking on masonry side. 3-7 day cure before painting. Do NOT use silicone — not paintable.

quality_notes.QT3: All masonry-to-trim joints caulked. Smooth tool. Clean edges.
quality_notes.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Mask both sides with stucco tape on masonry and blue tape on trim.

tasks.name: Surface Defect Repair
tasks.description: Patch spalled mortar, cracked mortar joints, bug holes in concrete, and surface defects. Masonry patching compound or hydraulic cement for structural repairs. Must be cured before coating.

quality_notes.QT3: Repair obvious defects and cracked mortar joints.
quality_notes.QT4: Repair all defects. Fill bug holes in concrete. Smooth patches to match surrounding texture where possible.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cure verification -> Moisture test (hard stop if >12%) -> Efflorescence treatment (if present, must complete before any coating) -> Power wash -> Dry time (24-48 hr) -> Form-release removal (concrete only) -> Surface defect repair -> Caulk masonry-to-trim joints -> Re-verify MC <12%.

sop_modules.name: CMU Block Filler Application
sop_modules.description: Apply block filler (PCA P12 Level 2 Standard Fill) to CMU surfaces. Fills voids to max 10 per SF. This is substrate preparation — NOT primer. Separate module because block filler is a distinct heavy-body material requiring different spray tip (527-535), filter (30-mesh), and higher PSI (2,300-3,000). Applied BEFORE alkali-resistant primer. CMU ONLY — not needed on brick, concrete, or limestone.

tasks.name: Block Filler — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply block filler by airless spray (527-535 tip, 30-mesh filter, 2,300-3,000 PSI) followed immediately by back-rolling with 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap roller. Back-rolling is MANDATORY — forces filler into CMU voids for continuous fill. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, roller follows while filler is wet. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_MSRY_BLOCK_FILLER.

quality_notes.all: Back-roll IMMEDIATELY while filler is wet. Roller must follow sprayer within 30-60 seconds. Force filler into all voids. No holidays or unfilled voids. Verify PCA P12 Level 2 standard: max 10 voids per SF after application.

tasks.name: Block Filler — Heavy Roller Application
tasks.description: Apply block filler by heavy roller (1-1/2 inch nap). Fallback method for smaller CMU areas or when spray is not practical. Work filler into all voids with heavy nap roller. Multiple passes may be needed to achieve fill. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_MSRY_BLOCK_FILLER.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to force filler into voids. Multiple passes if needed. Verify all voids filled. PCA P12 Level 2: max 10 voids per SF.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Applied AFTER prep module completes. Applied BEFORE primer module. Allow block filler to cure per product TDS (typically 4-8 hours) before primer application.

sop_modules.name: Alkali-Resistant Masonry Primer
sop_modules.description: Full field prime coat with alkali-resistant masonry primer. MANDATORY on ALL new masonry (pH 12-14) regardless of quality tier — this is not quality-optional. Primer rated to pH 13 (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer) enables 7-day accelerated coating schedule. Applied over block filler on CMU, directly to bare masonry on brick/concrete/limestone. Material system: SYS_EXT_MSRY_PRIMER_ALKALI. Oil-based primer is PROHIBITED.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant masonry primer by airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter, 1,500-2,500 PSI) followed immediately by back-rolling with 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap roller. Back-rolling forces primer into porous masonry surface for continuous protective film. Two-person operation. Single coat.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots. Back-roll immediately.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds of spray. Inspect for complete coverage.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Every pore saturated. Inspect under raking light on primary elevations.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant masonry primer by heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap). Work primer into all pores and surface texture. Single coat. Excellent mechanical bond — roller forces primer into masonry for superior adhesion.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to work primer into masonry pores. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Thick nap is essential — standard 3/8 inch nap will not penetrate masonry texture.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant masonry primer by brush. Detail work and small areas only — brush is never the primary method for masonry wall field. Work primer into mortar joints and surface texture.

quality_notes.all: Work primer into all mortar joints and surface texture. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single prime coat. Applied AFTER block filler on CMU, directly to bare masonry on brick/concrete/limestone. Allow primer to cure per product TDS before finish coat application.

sop_modules.name: Masonry Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat on primed masonry wall. Product determined by coating_system dimension: acrylic (SYS_EXT_MSRY_FINISH_ACRYLIC_STD at QT2/QT3, SYS_EXT_MSRY_FINISH_ACRYLIC_PREM at QT4) or elastomeric (SYS_EXT_MSRY_FINISH_ELASTOMERIC at QT3/QT4). Spray on masonry = ALWAYS spray_backroll (spray-only PROHIBITED). Back-rolling forces finish into porous texture for proper DFT.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by airless spray followed immediately by back-rolling. For acrylic: 517 tip, 60-mesh filter. For elastomeric: 531 tip, 30-mesh filter (heavy-body material). Back-rolling is MANDATORY on all masonry — forces finish into pores for continuous film and proper DFT. Two-person operation: sprayer leads, roller follows.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds. No holidays.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Consistent roller texture. No dry spots in mortar joints.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Every mortar joint and surface irregularity fully coated. Raking light check on visible elevations.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap). Fallback for smaller areas, occupied-adjacent, or when spray is not practical. Excellent mechanical bond on masonry. Extension poles for elevated work.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to work finish into masonry texture. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. For elastomeric: multiple heavy passes may be needed to achieve 20-30 mil DFT.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply first finish coat by brush. Detail work and small areas only. Work finish into mortar joints and surface texture.

quality_notes.all: Work finish into all mortar joints and surface texture. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: First finish coat. Applied after primer has cured. Spray_backroll is primary method — spray-only is PROHIBITED on masonry. Allow recoat time per product TDS before interstage/coat 2. QT2 acrylic may stop here (single finish coat on properly primed surface).

sop_modules.name: Masonry Interstage Inspection
sop_modules.description: Inspect first finish coat. Touch up defects. QT4 only: light 220 grit sand if surface anomalies detected (sand is unusual on textured masonry — inspect/touch-up is the primary interstage activity). Module skipped for QT2 single-coat acrylic systems.

tasks.name: Interstage Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for holidays, runs, sags, coverage defects, and missed mortar joints. For spray_backroll: verify uniform backroll texture and complete coverage in all voids. Check for pinholes indicating incomplete backroll.

quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough. Check all elevations for obvious defects — holidays, runs, missed joints.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Raking light inspection on visible elevations. Mark all defects. Check mortar joints and surface irregularities for complete coverage.

tasks.name: Interstage Light Sand (QT4 Only)
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats with 220 grit. QT4 only — rarely needed on textured masonry but required if surface anomalies detected during raking light inspection (runs, sags, nibs). Dust removal with tack cloth after sanding.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand on anomalies only. Do not attempt to sand entire textured masonry surface. Remove nibs and defects. Tack cloth dust removal before coat 2.

tasks.name: Interstage Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during interstage inspection. Focus on holidays, missed mortar joints, and coverage gaps.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix all defects found during inspection. Blend repairs into surrounding finish.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect -> Sand (QT4 only, if anomalies detected) -> Touch up -> Allow cure -> Coat 2. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat acrylic.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.

sop_modules.name: Masonry Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat. Required at QT3 and QT4 for acrylic, and mandatory for all elastomeric (2 coats required for 20-30 mil DFT). Skipped at QT2 acrylic (single coat acceptable on properly primed surface). Same application method as coat 1.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by airless spray + back-roll. Same method and configuration as coat 1. Critical for final appearance and total film build. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. No visible pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat. For elastomeric: verify DFT target 20-30 mils cumulative.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by heavy roller. Same method as coat 1. Final coat.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge. Final coat — critical for appearance.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) finish coat by brush. Detail work and small areas. Final coat.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Final coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Second and final finish coat. Same application method as coat 1. Skipped at QT2 acrylic. Elastomeric ALWAYS requires 2 coats (DFT target 20-30 mils).

sop_modules.name: Masonry Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough of completed masonry coating. Inspect all elevations. Holiday check with backlighting where possible. Touch up defects found.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished masonry for coverage consistency, holidays, and defects. Holiday check: use backlighting (late afternoon sun angle) on visible elevations to reveal thin spots and missed areas. Check mortar joints and surface irregularities for complete coverage.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for obvious misses.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check all elevations. Backlight check on primary elevation.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light and backlight check on all visible elevations. Document any defects for touch-up.

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Focus on holidays, thin spots, and mortar joint coverage.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly. Final sign-off.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect all elevations -> Touch up -> Sign off.

sop_modules.name: Masonry Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials, clean equipment, restore site.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all stucco tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers, and plastic sheeting. Check for tape residue on masonry (stucco tape can leave adhesive if overexposed to UV).

quality_notes.all: Check for tape residue. Remove all protection materials completely. Inspect landscape for overspray. Clean any overspray from hardscape immediately (easier when fresh).

tasks.name: Clean Equipment
tasks.description: Flush airless sprayer (full flush cycle — masonry coatings are abrasive). Clean tips and filters. Inspect tips for wear (cementitious substrates cause accelerated wear). Clean roller frames, dispose of saturated thick-nap covers. Clean brushes.

quality_notes.all: Full flush cycle for sprayer — block filler and elastomeric materials are especially important to flush completely. Tips and filters cleaned and stored. Roller covers disposed of properly.

tasks.name: Site Debris Cleanup
tasks.description: Collect all debris — caulk tubes, tape, plastic sheeting, paint cans, used roller covers, brush containers, sandpaper. Leave site clean.

quality_notes.all: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed. Check for staining on walkways/patios.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown -> Equipment cleaning -> Site cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Block Filler + Prime + 2 Finish Coats (CMU, QT3/QT4)
round_configurations.description: Full CMU sequence: 1 block filler + 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats.
round_configurations.notes: Block filler is phase=prep (substrate preparation, not a coating). 4 total applied layers: filler + primer + 2 finish. Elastomeric always requires 2 finish coats regardless of QT.

round_configurations.name: Block Filler + Prime + 1 Finish Coat (CMU, QT2)
round_configurations.description: Economy CMU sequence: 1 block filler + 1 primer + 1 finish coat.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy. Single acrylic finish coat on primed CMU. Elastomeric not available at QT2.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats (Brick/Concrete/Limestone, QT3/QT4)
round_configurations.description: Standard non-CMU sequence: 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 finish coats.
round_configurations.notes: No block filler needed for non-CMU masonry. Elastomeric always requires 2 finish coats.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (Brick/Concrete/Limestone, QT2)
round_configurations.description: Economy non-CMU sequence: 1 primer + 1 finish coat.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy. Single acrylic finish coat on primed masonry. Elastomeric not available at QT2.

key_masonry_rules_enforced: Spray on masonry = ALWAYS spray_backroll (spray-only PROHIBITED). Porous texture requires roller for proper DFT.
Crew size 2 for spray_backroll (one sprays, one follows with roller).
Block filler is a separate module BEFORE prime (CMU only).
Oil-based products PROHIBITED on all tasks — alkaline masonry causes saponification.
Moisture test is a hard stop (MC >12% = do not coat).
Efflorescence treatment must complete before any coating.
Alkali-resistant primer MANDATORY on ALL new masonry regardless of quality tier.
No acid cleaning on limestone substrate.

assumptions.value: Power washing IS allowed on masonry (unlike fiber cement and engineered wood)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Masonry_Brick_Block_CMU_Doctrine.md §4: 'Wash/power-wash; remove dust and loose paint' listed as PCA P14 Level 1 prep
assumptions.note: Masonry is dense and durable — power washing at 1,500-2,500 PSI does not damage surface. Distinct from fiber cement/engineered wood where power wash is prohibited.

assumptions.value: Spray on masonry = auto-add backroll. Spray-only is PROHIBITED on porous masonry.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6: 'Stucco and porous masonry: Spray bridges over pinholes/voids; back-rolling forces coating into pores'
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine. Applies to ALL coatings on masonry: block filler, primer, and finish.

assumptions.value: spray_backroll requires two-person crew (sprayer + roller operator)
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6 and Part B §8: 'Requires 2-person crew; coordination critical'
assumptions.note: Production rate impact: spray_backroll on masonry ~150-200 SF/hr vs spray-only 300-400 SF/hr. Estimation Engineer must account for two-person crew.

assumptions.value: Red stucco poly tape required instead of standard blue tape for masking ON masonry surfaces
assumptions.note: Exterior_Protection_Doctrine does not specifically address tape selection for rough masonry surfaces. Standard blue tape does not adhere to textured masonry. Stucco tape is the field-standard solution.

assumptions.value: Efflorescence treatment is a site-condition-gated task (include_when efflorescence_present)
assumptions.note: Doctrine describes efflorescence treatment procedures but does not define it as a formal site_condition_id. Using 'efflorescence_present' as condition with values light/moderate/severe. Flag for Site_Condition_Vocabulary addition.

assumptions.value: Hot surface temperature blocks finish application — substrate pre-wetting may be needed in high heat
assumptions.source: Exterior_Climate_Environmental_Conditions_Doctrine.md §5: 'Lightly misting masonry surface with water before application prevents substrate from stealing moisture from coating'
assumptions.note: SOP-level procedure note. Porous masonry wicks water from paint film in high heat causing flash drying and poor adhesion.

assumptions.value: Light sanding between coats is unusual on textured masonry — QT4 only, and only if anomalies detected
assumptions.source: Research and field practice; confirmed by resolution.json interstage module notes
assumptions.note: Doctrine is silent on whether interstage sanding applies to textured masonry. Unlike smooth interior surfaces, masonry texture makes full-surface sanding impractical. Sand only on anomalies (runs, sags, nibs).
